캡션(한국어): 자진산염불은 황해도 지방의 서도민요로, 느린 긴염불과 빠른 자진염불이 조화를 이루며 인생의 무상함과 그리움을 표현하는 민속악의 대표적인 곡이다. 여창 가창자 유지숙은 이 곡에서 서정적인 내용의 멜로디를 통해 깊은 감정을 전달하며, 그녀의 목소리는 섬세하게 곡의 흐름을 이끌어간다. 유지숙은 발성을 통해 긴 호흡을 유지하며, 시김새를 적절히 사용하여 멜로디의 변화를 부드럽게 연결한다. 그녀의 성량은 곡의 전개에 따라 변화하며, 각 구절의 강조를 통해 청중의 주의를 끌고, 호흡의 리듬감을 통해 자연스러운 흐름을 만들어낸다. 굿거리 장단의 리듬 속에서 가창자는 세심하게 박자를 타며, 그녀의 호흡은 곡의 마무리 부분에서 여운을 남기고, 전체적인 장르의 완성도를 높이는 역할을 한다. 이러한 방식으로 유지숙은 자진산염불의 감성을 고스란히 전달하며, 청중에게 깊은 여운을 남긴다.
캡션(영어): Jajin san yeombul is a representative piece of folk music from the western coastal region of Hwanghaedo, characterized by a harmonious blend of the slow long yeombul and the fast jajin yeombul, expressing the transience of life and longing. The vocalist Yoo Ji-sook conveys profound emotions through a lyrical melody in this piece, with her voice delicately guiding the flow of the music. Yoo maintains a long breath through her vocalization, skillfully employing variations in pitch to smoothly connect the changes in melody. Her vocal strength varies throughout the progression of the piece, capturing the audience's attention through the emphasis of each phrase and creating a natural flow with the rhythm of her breath. Within the rhythm of the gutgeori jangdan, the singer meticulously keeps the beat, and her breath leaves a lingering resonance in the concluding section of the piece, enhancing the overall quality of the genre. In this manner, Yoo Ji-sook effectively conveys the emotions of jajin san yeombul, leaving a deep impression on the audience.

캡션(영어): Byeongsin Nanbongga is a folk song that has been passed down in the Hwanghae Province and is one of the representative pieces of the Seodo folk songs. This piece features a unique structure where it is sung in succession with Jajin Nanbongga, Byeongsin Nanbongga, and Sasel Nanbongga, with the tempo accelerating as it progresses. The voice of the female vocalist Yoo Ji-sook effectively highlights the characteristics of this song, as she powerfully belts out high notes during the lyrical sections to create tension, while maintaining a serene flow in the chorus with mid-range tones that seamlessly connect the song's progression. Yoo Ji-sook leads the development of the piece through her vocalization and ornamentation, particularly expressing the five-note structure of Nanbongga Tori, which consists of La, Do, Re, Mi, and Sol. Riding on the rhythm of the Gutgeori Jangdan, the vocalist navigates the flow of the song, controlling her breath to clearly delineate the changes between verses and choruses. This breath control embellishes the conclusion of the piece and contributes to enhancing the genre's overall completeness within Seodo folk songs.

캡션(영어): Geumdeureong Taryeong is a new folk song from the genre of Nambongga that emerged in Hwanghaedo after the Enlightenment period, and it is a part of the folk music that distinctly showcases the characteristics of Seodominyo. This piece sings of the transience of life and the sorrow of love, with the unique refrain of "Geumdeureong Geumdeureong" creating a distinctive rhythm. Female vocalist Kim Min-kyung vividly conveys the emotions of the song through her performance, and her voice gently guides the melody. Her vocalization is precise and stable, effectively highlighting the elements of traditional folk music through her use of sigimsae. Kim Min-kyung articulates each syllable clearly, seamlessly maintaining the flow of the piece. Her vocal range flexibly adapts to the development of the song, and her breath control is exceptional, allowing her to sustain long notes steadily. Riding on the rhythm of the Gutgeori Jangdan, Kim Min-kyung navigates the flow of the piece at her own tempo, skillfully enhancing the rhythmic quality of her singing. Her breath elegantly adorns the conclusion of the song, contributing to the overall completeness of the genre.

캡션(한국어): 산천가는 북한의 명창 김진명이 작사, 작곡한 신민요로, 해방 후 농촌의 풍요로움과 산천의 아름다움을 경쾌하게 노래한 곡이다. 이 곡은 서도민요의 특징이 잘 드러나는 민속악 장르에 속하며, 전통적인 민요의 형식을 유지하면서도 현대적인 감각이 가미된 점이 돋보인다. 여창 가창자 유지숙의 목소리는 이 곡을 이끌어가는 중요한 요소로, 그녀는 경쾌한 분위기를 잘 표현하며 곡 전체에 활력을 불어넣는다. 유지숙은 발성을 통해 멜로디의 흐름을 자연스럽게 이어가고, 시김새를 적절히 사용하여 곡의 전통적인 감성을 강조한다. 그녀의 성량은 곡의 리듬에 잘 맞추어져 있으며, 호흡을 조절하여 각 구절의 끝을 부드럽게 마무리한다. 이러한 창법은 곡의 경쾌한 분위기를 더욱 부각시키며, 청중이 자연스럽게 흥미를 느끼도록 만든다. 굿거리의 리듬 위에서 가창자는 안정적으로 흐름을 타며, 호흡을 통해 곡의 마무리를 장식하고 장르적 완성도를 높인다. 유지숙의 목소리는 이러한 리듬과 잘 어우러져, 듣는 이로 하여금 산천의 아름다움과 농촌의 풍요로움을 생생하게 느끼게 한다.
캡션(영어): Sancheongana is a new folk song written and composed by the renowned North Korean singer Kim Jin-myung, which joyfully celebrates the richness of rural life and the beauty of nature after liberation. This piece belongs to the folk music genre that distinctly showcases the characteristics of Seodo minyo, and it stands out for incorporating a modern sensibility while maintaining the traditional form of folk songs. The voice of the female vocalist Yoo Ji-sook is a crucial element that drives this piece, as she effectively expresses a lively atmosphere and infuses vitality throughout the song. Yoo Ji-sook seamlessly connects the flow of the melody through her vocalization, employing appropriate vocal embellishments to emphasize the traditional sentiment of the piece. Her vocal range aligns well with the rhythm of the song, and she skillfully controls her breath to gently conclude each phrase. This singing technique further accentuates the lively mood of the piece, allowing the audience to naturally feel engaged. Riding on the rhythm of the gutgeori, the vocalist maintains a stable flow, using her breath to embellish the conclusion of the piece and enhance its genre-specific completeness. Yoo Ji-sook's voice harmonizes well with this rhythm, enabling listeners to vividly experience the beauty of nature and the richness of rural life.

This piece celebrates the happiness of a bountiful catch and is also referred to as "Bongjuk Taryeong," encapsulating the spirit and elation of fishermen. The voice of the female vocalist Jang Hyo-seon serves as the primary means of expression for this song, and her singing style effectively embodies the characteristics of traditional Seodo folk music. Through her vocalization, Jang Hyo-seon naturally guides the rhythm and melody of the piece, employing appropriate techniques to convey the song's emotions. Her vocal power strongly supports the flow of the music, while her breath control adapts flexibly to the development of the melody. Notably, over the gutgeori jangdan, Jang Hyo-seon rides the rhythm, clearly revealing the structure of the piece, and her breath management gracefully embellishes the conclusion of the song. These elements enhance the traditional completeness of Baechigi and convey the allure of Seodo folk music in a more profound manner.

캡션(한국어): 금다래꿍은 황해도 황주 지방의 전설을 바탕으로 한 서도민요로, 수심가토리와 창부타령토리가 결합된 독특한 음계가 특징이다. 이 곡은 사랑하는 연인을 만나러 가는 설렘을 경쾌하게 표현하며, 민속악 중에서도 민요 장르에 속한다. 여창 가창자 김민경의 목소리는 이 곡의 흐름을 이끌어가는 중요한 요소로 작용한다. 그녀는 발성을 통해 곡의 멜로디를 섬세하게 표현하며, 시김새를 적절히 사용하여 전통적인 서도민요의 맛을 살린다. 성량은 곡의 리듬에 맞춰 자연스럽게 조절되며, 굿거리장단의 경쾌한 리듬을 따라 유연하게 흐른다. 호흡 또한 중요하게 작용하여, 각 구절의 마무리를 부드럽게 장식하며 전체적인 곡의 완성도를 높인다. 이러한 요소들이 결합되어 김민경의 목소리는 금다래꿍의 서사적 매력을 극대화하며, 청중에게 전통 민요의 깊이를 전달한다.
캡션(영어): Geumdaraekkung is a Western Korean folk song based on legends from the Hwangju region of Hwanghae Province, characterized by a unique scale that combines the Sushim gatari and Changbu talyeong. This piece expressively captures the excitement of going to meet a beloved, and it belongs to the genre of folk music within traditional music. The voice of female vocalist Kim Min-kyung serves as a crucial element that guides the flow of the piece. Through her vocalization, she delicately articulates the melody while appropriately employing sigimsae to preserve the traditional flavor of Western Korean folk songs. Her vocal volume is naturally adjusted to align with the rhythm of the piece, flowing flexibly along with the lively rhythm of the gutgeori jangdan. Breath control also plays an important role, gracefully embellishing the endings of each phrase and enhancing the overall completeness of the composition. These elements combine to maximize the narrative charm of Geumdaraekkung through Kim Min-kyung's voice, conveying the depth of traditional folk music to the audience.

캡션(영어): Gaeseong Nanbongga is a folk song from the Gaeseong region, known by the name "Parkyeon Waterfall," which embodies a blend of characteristics from Seodo sori and Gyeonggi sori. This piece is joyfully sung in accordance with the Guttari Jangdan, celebrating the breathtaking scenery of Parkyeon Waterfall and expressing love, while effectively conveying the unique atmosphere of the Gaeseong region, showcasing the charm of Seodo minyo. The voice of female vocalist Kim Min-kyung serves as a crucial element in leading this piece, as her vocalization elevates the energy of the song and leaves a strong impression on the listener. Kim Min-kyung skillfully employs vocal embellishments to express the melody and drives the development of the piece with her powerful voice. Her breath control harmonizes well with the rhythm of the song, playing a significant role in riding the lively flow of the Guttari. This control of breath enhances the conclusion of the piece and contributes to the overall genre's completeness. Kim Min-kyung's singing further accentuates the allure of Parkyeon Waterfall, providing the audience with a profound emotional experience.

캡션(영어): Jajinari is a genre of Seodo folk song that originated from agricultural labor songs in the Yonggang region of South Pyongan Province and has evolved into a popular folk song through the efforts of professional singers. Musically, it is based on the Su-sim-ga-tori and is characterized by a transition from a slow Giniari to a lively Gukgeori or Taryeong Jangdan, which is performed at a faster tempo. This piece embodies the dual nature of work songs and playful songs, and is traditionally performed in conjunction with Giniari as a refined example of Seodo popular folk music. The voice of female vocalist Yoo Ji-sook plays a crucial role in leading this piece, and her singing style harmonizes well with the lively rhythm of the Gukgeori Jangdan. Yoo Ji-sook clarifies the structure of the song through her vocalization, skillfully employing embellishments to highlight the characteristics of traditional folk music. She modulates her vocal volume to express a rhythmic melody and seamlessly connects the flow of the piece through her breath control. Her voice flows briskly over the rhythm of the Gukgeori, adjusting her breath at the end of each phrase to embellish the conclusion of the piece and enhance its overall artistic completeness.

캡션(영어): Jajin Nanbongga is a genre of folk song that has been passed down in the Hwanghae Province, classified under the category of minyo, which is a form of traditional folk music. This piece features a sequence of singing styles including Jajin Nanbongga, Byeongsin Nanbongga, and Saseol Nanbongga, characterized by an increasing tempo as it progresses into the latter half. The voice of the female vocalist Yu Jisook plays a crucial role in the development of the piece, particularly in the refrain section where she employs various vocal techniques to modulate the tension of the song, either belting out high notes or delivering low tones with a gentle inflection. At the beginning of Jajin Nanbongga, she powerfully sings the phrase "neomeoganda neomeo neomeoganda," setting an intense tone for the piece. Throughout the refrain, she maintains a high vocal range, capturing the audience's attention, while skillfully utilizing sigimsae to ensure a smooth flow of the music. Her voice flows flexibly over the rhythm of the Gutgeori jangdan, culminating the piece with her breath control, thereby enhancing the overall artistic quality of the genre. Yu Jisook's vocalization and breath management effectively convey the rhythmic essence of the song, leaving a profound impression on the audience.

캡션(영어): Neurigae Taryeong is a folk music piece that embodies the traditions of Seodo Minyo, representing a type of work song that has been passed down in the Eunyul region. This piece begins with a collective recitation and features a structure where a soloist continues the melody, composed in a strophic form with a refrain and four verses. It progresses in accordance with the Gutgeori Jangdan, with four beats forming a single section. The melody is structured in a pentatonic scale similar to Gyeonggi Minyo, and while the characteristics of the melody are known to be reminiscent of Hwanghaedo folk songs, there are also similarities to the sounds of Gyeonggi Province. The voice of female vocalist Kim Min-kyung serves as a crucial element guiding the flow of the piece. Through her vocalization, she clearly articulates the structure of the song and effectively employs stylistic nuances that highlight the characteristics of traditional folk music. Her vocal volume is appropriately controlled, and her breath is stable, effectively embellishing the ends of each section. Kim Min-kyung flows flexibly with the rhythm of the Gutgeori, seamlessly connecting the tempo of each phrase. Her breath plays an important role in the conclusion of the piece, contributing to the overall genre's completeness. These elements combine to make Neurigae Taryeong a piece that effectively conveys the charm of traditional folk music.

캡션(한국어): 삼동주타령은 서도소리에 속하는 민요로, 봄의 생동감과 경쾌한 분위기를 담고 있는 곡이다. 이 곡은 굿거리풍의 장단으로 부르며, 따뜻한 봄날의 정취를 서도 특유의 창법으로 표현한 민속악의 중요한 예시로 자리잡고 있다. 여창 가창자 유지숙의 목소리는 이 곡의 매력을 한층 더 끌어올리며, 그녀의 콧소리 나는 음색은 서도민요의 전통적인 요소를 잘 살리고 있다. 유지숙은 멜로디를 부를 때, 고유의 발성 기법과 시김새를 활용하여 곡의 정서를 풍부하게 전달한다. 그녀의 성량은 곡의 흐름에 따라 유연하게 변화하며, 강약 조절이 뛰어나 청중에게 깊은 인상을 남긴다. 호흡 또한 곡의 리듬에 잘 맞춰져 있어, 긴 음을 끌거나 짧게 끊는 방식으로 굿거리 장단의 경쾌함을 효과적으로 표현한다. 이러한 호흡과 발성의 조화는 곡의 마무리에서도 돋보이며, 유지숙의 목소리는 리듬의 흐름을 타고 자연스럽게 이어지며 곡의 완성도를 높인다.
캡션(영어): Samdongjutaryeong is a folk song belonging to the Seodo style, encapsulating the vibrancy and cheerful atmosphere of spring. This piece is performed in the Gukgeori style of Jangdan, serving as an important example of folk music that expresses the essence of a warm spring day through the unique vocal technique characteristic of Seodo. The voice of the female vocalist Yoo Ji-sook enhances the charm of this piece, and her nasal timbre effectively preserves the traditional elements of Seodo folk songs. When singing the melody, Yoo utilizes her distinctive vocal techniques and ornamentation to convey the song's emotions richly. Her vocal range flexibly adapts to the flow of the piece, exhibiting excellent control over dynamics that leaves a deep impression on the audience. Additionally, her breathing aligns well with the rhythm of the song, effectively expressing the liveliness of the Gukgeori Jangdan by either extending long notes or cutting them short. This harmony of breath and vocalization is particularly prominent in the conclusion of the piece, where Yoo's voice seamlessly follows the rhythmic flow, enhancing the overall completeness of the song.

캡션(영어): Saseol Nanbongga is a humorous and playful long narrative song belonging to the genre of Seodo Minyo, which is a form of folk music. This piece is characterized by its rapid delivery in accordance with the Bokkneun Taryeong Jangdan, and its lyrics, filled with witty anecdotes and humor, stand out as a means to engage the audience. The voice of the female vocalist Yoo Ji-sook enhances the charm of the piece, as she effectively captures the lively rhythm through her vocalization and demonstrates her ability to swiftly navigate the lengthy narrative. Yoo Ji-sook appropriately employs vocal embellishments to emphasize the folk elements, while also conveying the humor embedded in the lyrics. Her vocal volume is adjusted in accordance with the progression of the piece, and her breath control maintains a stable and balanced flow. Riding the rhythm of Jajinmori, Yoo Ji-sook seamlessly follows the flow of the song, and in the final section of her performance, she elegantly concludes the piece through her breath. These elements combine to elevate the artistic completeness of Saseol Nanbongga, leaving a profound impression on the audience.

캡션(한국어): 간장타령은 사람의 간장과 먹는 간장을 언어유희적으로 대비시킨 신민요로, 서도민요의 특성이 잘 드러나는 민속악의 한 예이다. 이 곡은 애절한 사랑을 주제로 하면서도 해학적인 가사를 통해 슬픔을 웃음으로 승화시키는 특징을 가지고 있다. 여창 가창자 김민경의 목소리는 이 곡의 감정을 이끌어가는 중요한 요소로, 그녀는 서도 창법을 통해 독특한 발성과 시김새를 구사한다. 김민경은 고음과 저음을 자유롭게 오가며 멜로디를 표현하고, 각 음절에 적절한 강조를 주어 곡의 흐름을 자연스럽게 이어간다. 그녀의 성량은 곡의 전개에 따라 조절되며, 호흡은 적절한 시점에서 이루어져 긴장감과 여유를 동시에 전달한다. 이 곡의 기반이 되는 세마치풍과 중모리의 리듬 위에서 김민경은 리드미컬하게 흐름을 타며, 그녀의 호흡은 곡의 마무리를 부드럽게 장식하고 장르적 완성도를 높인다. 이러한 요소들이 결합되어 간장타령은 서도민요의 매력을 잘 드러내는 곡으로 완성된다.
캡션(영어): Ganjang Taryeong is a new folk song that playfully contrasts the human liver with soy sauce, exemplifying the characteristics of Seodo minyo. This piece, centered on the theme of poignant love, possesses the unique ability to transform sorrow into laughter through its humorous lyrics. The voice of the female vocalist Kim Min-kyung serves as a crucial element in conveying the emotions of the song, as she employs the Seodo singing style to execute distinctive vocal techniques and embellishments. Kim Min-kyung navigates freely between high and low notes to express the melody, providing appropriate emphasis on each syllable to ensure a natural flow throughout the piece. Her vocal volume is adjusted according to the progression of the song, and her breath control occurs at suitable moments, simultaneously conveying tension and ease. Riding on the rhythms of semachi-pung and jungmori, Kim Min-kyung flows rhythmically, and her breath gracefully embellishes the conclusion of the piece, enhancing its genre-specific completeness. These elements combine to make Ganjang Taryeong a well-crafted representation of the charm of Seodo minyo.

캡션(영어): ‘Nalchane’ is a piece of folk music transmitted as a Seodo Japga, which distinctly showcases the characteristics of Seodo Minyo, a traditional music genre from the Hwanghae Province. This piece maintains the traditional form of folk songs while incorporating unique elements of Seodo Japga, strongly reflecting regional identity. The voice of the female vocalist Jang Hyo-seon is a crucial element that drives the piece, as her singing style naturally expresses the melody with rich embellishments. Jang Hyo-seon clearly conveys the melody through distinct tonal differentiation in her vocalization, with the pronunciation of each syllable organically connected to the flow of the piece. Her breath provides stability in navigating long phrases, flexibly adapting to the rhythms of Jungmori and Semachi. Over these rhythmic elements, Jang Hyo-seon’s voice enriches the overall structure of the piece, and her breath plays an important role in embellishing the conclusion of the song. This emphasizes the charm of traditional Seodo Minyo and contributes to the genre's overall completeness.

캡션(영어): Ginnanbongga is a type of Seodo minyo that originated in the Hwanghae Province and has been widely sung since the late Joseon period. This piece is structured in suhimgatari and features a repetitive verse form with 11 verses and a refrain, effectively showcasing the characteristics of Seodo minyo. The voice of the female vocalist Yoo Ji-sook brings out the essence of this piece, and her vocalization adheres faithfully to traditional singing techniques. Yoo Ji-sook extends the notes while expressing the melody with flexibility, and she appropriately employs embellishments to convey the emotions of the song. Her vocal power is stable, and her breath seamlessly connects the flow of the piece, allowing it to unfold rhythmically in accordance with the Jungmori jangdan. Yoo Ji-sook's breath adorns the conclusion of the piece, contributing to the overall completeness of the traditional folk song. These elements combine to establish Ginnanbongga as a piece that well represents the charm of Seodo minyo.

캡션(영어): Ssalum Taryeong is a form of folk song from Hwanghae Province, derived from the dialect term 'ssalum,' which refers to the 'cricket.' This piece effectively showcases the characteristics of Seodo Minyo, encapsulating a sense of longing for one's hometown and a poignant emotional depth. The mournful melody flows throughout the composition, possessing the charm of lyrical folk music that resonates with the listener's heart. The voice of the female vocalist Jang Hyo-seon forms the centerpiece of this piece, with her vocal delivery conveying the melody in a stable and clear manner. Jang Hyo-seon skillfully employs traditional ornamentation while focusing on expressing the emotions of the song. Her vocal volume is adjusted appropriately according to the flow of the piece, and her breath is seamlessly integrated, aligning well with the rhythm. 캡션(한국어): 호무가는 평안북도 지방의 김매기 소리로, '호미타령'과는 구분되는 서도민요의 대표적인 예로, 농경 문화와 지역적 특색을 잘 보여주는 민속악 > 민요 곡이다. 이 곡은 선후창 형식으로 부르며, 향토적인 색채가 짙어 해당 지역의 전통과 정서를 고스란히 담고 있다. 여창 가창자 장효선의 목소리는 이 곡의 중요한 요소로, 콧소리 나는 음색을 통해 독특한 매력을 발산한다. 그녀의 발성은 명확하고 힘차며, 시김새를 적절히 활용하여 멜로디의 흐름을 자연스럽게 이끌어간다. 장효선은 곡의 리듬과 구조에 맞춰 성량을 조절하며, 호흡을 통해 멜로디의 각 구절을 부드럽게 연결한다. 굿거리의 리듬 위에서 그녀의 목소리는 유연하게 흐르며, 각 음절의 길이를 조절하여 곡의 긴장감과 완성도를 높인다. 특히, 호흡의 조절은 곡의 마무리에서 중요한 역할을 하여, 전반적인 리듬과의 조화를 이루며 청중에게 깊은 인상을 남긴다.
캡션(영어): Homuga is a representative example of Seodo folk songs, distinct from 'Homitarang,' characterized by the sound of rice planting in the North Pyongan Province. This folk song effectively showcases agricultural culture and regional characteristics. It is performed in a call-and-response format, imbued with a strong local flavor that captures the traditions and emotions of the area. The voice of the female vocalist Jang Hyo-seon is a crucial element of this piece, exuding a unique charm through her nasal timbre. Her vocalization is clear and powerful, skillfully employing ornamentation to guide the flow of the melody naturally. Jang Hyo-seon adjusts her vocal volume in accordance with the rhythm and structure of the song, seamlessly connecting each phrase of the melody through her breath. Over the rhythmic foundation of gutgeori, her voice flows flexibly, manipulating the length of each syllable to enhance the song's tension and overall quality. Notably, her breath control plays a vital role in the conclusion of the piece, achieving harmony with the overall rhythm and leaving a profound impression on the audience.

캡션(한국어): 평안도 모내기는 평안도 지역에서 전해지는 전통적인 모내기 노동요로, 서도민요의 특성을 잘 나타내는 민속악의 한 형태이다. 이 곡은 평안도 항두게놀이의 제3장인 '모내기'에서 불리며, 농사와 관련된 노동의 소리를 담고 있다. 여창 가창자 장효선의 목소리는 이 곡을 이끌어가는 중요한 요소로, 그녀의 발성이 곡의 주제를 효과적으로 전달한다. 장효선은 전통적인 창법을 사용하여 멜로디를 표현하며, 시김새를 적절히 활용하여 곡의 흐름을 자연스럽게 이어간다. 그녀의 성량은 곡의 전개에 따라 유동적으로 변화하며, 호흡의 조절이 뛰어나 곡의 긴장감과 이완을 적절히 조화시킨다. 특히 굿거리 장단 위에서 그녀의 목소리는 리듬을 타며 흐름을 형성하고, 각 구절의 끝부분에서 호흡을 잘 조절하여 곡의 마무리를 장식한다. 이러한 요소들은 장효선의 가창이 곡의 장르적 완성도를 높이는 데 기여하며, 전통적인 민속악의 매력을 잘 드러낸다.
캡션(영어): Pyeongando Monaegi is a traditional rice planting labor song that has been passed down in the Pyeongando region, representing a form of folk music that embodies the characteristics of Seodominyo. This piece is sung in the third section titled 'Monaegi' of the Pyeongando Hangduge Nori, encapsulating the sounds associated with agricultural labor. The voice of the female vocalist Jang Hyo-seon is a crucial element that drives this piece, as her vocalization effectively conveys the theme of the song. Jang Hyo-seon employs traditional singing techniques to express the melody, skillfully utilizing ornamentation to create a natural flow throughout the piece. Her vocal range dynamically shifts according to the development of the song, demonstrating excellent breath control that harmonizes tension and relaxation. Particularly over the Gutgeori Jangdan, her voice rides the rhythm, shaping the flow and artfully managing her breath at the ends of phrases to embellish the conclusion of the piece. These elements contribute to Jang Hyo-seon's performance, enhancing the genre's completeness and showcasing the allure of traditional folk music.

캡션(한국어): 평안도 자진모내기는 평안도 지역에서 전해지는 전통적인 모내기 노동요로, 서도민요의 특징이 잘 드러나는 민속악의 한 형태이다. 이 곡은 평안도 항두게놀이의 제3장 ‘모내기’에서 불리는 민요로, 노동의 기쁨과 공동체의 화합을 담고 있다. 여창 가창자 장효선의 목소리는 이 곡을 이끌어가는 중심 요소로, 그녀의 발성은 전통적인 창법을 기반으로 하여 자연스러운 음의 흐름을 유지한다. 장효선은 곡의 멜로디를 표현하는 데 있어 전통적인 시김새를 적절히 사용하여 곡의 리듬과 감정을 전달한다. 그녀의 성량은 곡의 각 부분에 맞춰 조절되며, 호흡의 흐름이 부드럽게 이어져 곡 전체에 일관성을 부여한다. 특히 자진모리의 경쾌한 리듬 위에서 장효선은 정확한 박자감과 함께 곡의 진행을 잘 타며, 각 음절마다 명확한 발음을 통해 청중에게 메시지를 전달한다. 그녀의 호흡은 곡의 마무리 부분에서 특히 중요한 역할을 하며, 긴장감을 유지하면서도 자연스럽게 풀어지는 느낌을 준다. 이러한 요소들은 곡의 장르적 완성도를 높이며, 전통적인 민속악의 매력을 더욱 부각시킨다.
캡션(영어): The Pyeongan-do Jajinmonaegi is a traditional rice planting labor song that has been passed down in the Pyeongan-do region, representing a form of folk music that distinctly showcases the characteristics of Seodo minyo. This piece is sung in the third section, "Monaegi," of the Pyeongan-do Hangduge Nori, encapsulating the joy of labor and the harmony of the community. The voice of the female vocalist Jang Hyo-seon serves as a central element guiding the piece, with her vocalization maintaining a natural flow of sound based on traditional singing techniques. Jang Hyo-seon appropriately employs traditional sigimsae to express the melody of the song, conveying its rhythm and emotions effectively. Her vocal range is adjusted to fit each section of the piece, with a smooth continuity of breath that lends consistency to the entire composition. Particularly over the lively rhythm of Jajinmori, Jang Hyo-seon navigates the progression of the piece with precise sense of timing, delivering the message to the audience through clear enunciation of each syllable. Her breath plays a crucial role in the concluding part of the song, maintaining tension while also providing a sense of natural release. These elements enhance the genre's overall completeness and further highlight the charm of traditional folk music.

The voice of the female vocalist Yoo Ji-sook guides the flow of the piece, with her vocalization distinctly and clearly expressing the melody. Yoo Ji-sook employs traditional singing techniques while effectively utilizing embellishments to convey the emotions of the song, and her vocal strength flexibly adjusts according to the progression of the piece. Her breathing is stable, seamlessly aligning with the rhythm of the song, which aids the audience in following the flow. Over the brisk rhythm of Jajinmori, the vocalist powerfully articulates each phrase, concluding the piece with a flourish through controlled breathing. These elements enhance the genre's overall completeness and further emphasize the charm of traditional folk music.

캡션(영어): Baekkkot Taryeong is a folk song from the Seo-do region of Hwanghae Province, celebrating the beauty of a maiden likened to pear blossoms. This piece is influenced by the musical style of Gyeonggi music and the sounds of Sadangpae, encapsulating the essence of a vibrant spring day and the emotions of love. As a representative example of the folk music genre, which highlights the characteristics of Seo-do folk songs, this piece is further enhanced by the voice of female vocalist Yoo Ji-sook. Yoo Ji-sook gracefully leads the melody, showcasing her technique by effortlessly navigating between high and low tones. Her singing style appropriately utilizes embellishments to preserve the traditional flavor of the folk song, while her vocal volume is adjusted to match the flow of the piece. Her breathing is stable, allowing her to take breaths at necessary moments, seamlessly connecting the rhythm of the melody. Riding on the rhythm of the gutgeori, Yoo Ji-sook captivates the audience with her flexible expressiveness in accordance with the rhythm. Her breath adorns the climax and conclusion of the piece, serving as a crucial element that enhances the overall quality of the traditional folk song.

캡션(한국어): 통영개타령은 경상도 지역의 향토민요인 개타령을 바탕으로 한 통속화된 민요로, 밤에 찾아오는 임을 위해 개에게 짖지 말라고 부탁하는 내용을 해학적으로 표현하고 있다. 이 곡은 경상도민요의 특유의 투박하면서도 정겨운 맛을 잘 드러내는 민속악의 한 예로, 지역적 정서를 담고 있다. 여창 가창자 김민지는 이 곡을 통해 전통적인 창법을 활용하여 곡의 이야기를 생동감 있게 전달한다. 그녀의 목소리는 강하고 또렷하며, 발성에서 나타나는 시김새는 전통 민요의 특징을 잘 살린다. 김민지는 고음과 저음을 자유롭게 넘나들며, 각 음의 길이를 조절하여 리듬감을 부여하고, 곡의 흐름을 자연스럽게 이끈다. 그녀의 성량은 곡의 다양한 구간에서 적절히 조절되며, 호흡의 조절도 뛰어나 곡의 긴장감과 여유를 동시에 표현한다. 자진모리의 경쾌한 리듬 위에서 김민지는 유연하게 흐름을 타며, 각 마디마다의 변화에 맞춰 목소리를 조율한다. 곡의 마무리에서는 호흡이 안정되며, 마지막 음을 길게 끌어주어 청중에게 여운을 남기고, 전통적인 민요의 완성도를 높이는 데 기여한다.
캡션(영어): Tongyeong Gaetaryeong is a popularized folk song based on the local Gyeongsang-do folk song Gaetaryeong, humorously expressing the plea to a dog not to bark for the beloved who comes at night. This piece exemplifies the unique rustic yet endearing qualities of Gyeongsang-do folk music, encapsulating regional sentiments. The female vocalist Kim Min-ji utilizes traditional singing techniques to vividly convey the story of the song. Her voice is strong and clear, and the ornamentation in her vocalization effectively highlights the characteristics of traditional folk songs. Kim Min-ji effortlessly navigates between high and low notes, adjusting the length of each note to create a sense of rhythm and guide the flow of the piece naturally. Her vocal volume is appropriately modulated throughout various sections of the song, and her breath control is exceptional, allowing her to express both tension and ease simultaneously. Riding on the lively rhythm of Jajinmori, Kim Min-ji fluidly adapts her voice to match the changes in each measure. In the conclusion of the piece, her breath stabilizes, and she extends the final note, leaving a lingering impression on the audience and contributing to the overall completeness of the traditional folk song.

캡션(영어): Miryang Arirang is a representative folk song from the Miryang region of Gyeongsang Province, characterized by the lively rhythm of the semachi jangdan and the lyrics "nal jom boso." This piece effectively showcases the typical elements of Gyeongsang folk songs and expresses the vibrant and spirited temperament of the local residents. The voice of the female vocalist Seong Seul-gi is a crucial element that drives the song, as she articulates the melody clearly through traditional singing techniques. Seong Seul-gi naturally navigates the high vocal range in her delivery and employs appropriate vocal embellishments to evoke a folk sensibility. Her vocal strength harmonizes well with the rhythm of the piece, demonstrating her skill in seamlessly connecting long phrases through breath control. Notably, over the lively rhythm of the semachi jangdan, Seong Seul-gi rides the flow of the song, flexibly adjusting her voice to match the rhythm. Her breath leaves a lingering resonance at the conclusion of the piece, contributing to the overall completeness of the traditional folk song.

캡션(한국어): 「상주모심기노래」는 경상도 민요로, 전형적인 메나리 토리의 특징을 지닌 민속악의 일환이다. 이 곡은 경상북도 상주의 ‘공갈못’이라는 역사적인 저수지와 관련이 있으며, 그 지역의 문화적 배경과 함께 청혼, 시집살이의 어려움, 농사의 고됨 등을 주제로 다양한 이야기를 담고 있다. 경상도민요는 메나리조의 노래가 많고, 노동요가 주를 이루며, 씩씩하고 꿋꿋한 느낌을 주는 것이 특징이다. 여창 가창자 김민지는 이 곡을 통해 목소리로 민요의 전통을 이어간다. 그녀의 발성은 명확하고 힘이 있으며, 시김새를 통해 곡의 정서를 섬세하게 표현한다. 특히, 그녀는 메나리조의 특성을 살려서 멜로디를 유연하게 구사하며, 각 음절의 강조를 통해 청중의 귀를 사로잡는다. 성량이 풍부하여 곡의 다양한 구간에서 안정적인 음역대를 유지하며, 호흡을 조절하여 긴장감과 여유를 동시에 느끼게 한다. 중모리의 리듬 위에서 김민지는 곡의 흐름을 자연스럽게 타고, 리듬에 맞춰 목소리를 적절히 변주하며 곡의 매력을 더욱 부각시킨다. 그녀의 호흡은 곡의 마무리를 장식하며, 전체적인 장르적 완성도를 높이는 데 기여한다.
캡션(영어): The "Sangju Mosimgi Nore" is a folk song from Gyeongsang-do, characterized by the typical features of the Menari style, and is part of the traditional music repertoire. This piece is associated with the historical reservoir known as "Gonggalmot" in Sangju, Gyeongsangbuk-do, and it encompasses various narratives reflecting the cultural background of the region, including themes of courtship, the hardships of married life, and the toil of farming. Gyeongsang-do folk songs are abundant in Menari-style melodies, predominantly consisting of labor songs, and are noted for their vigorous and resilient character. The female vocalist Kim Min-ji carries on the tradition of folk music through her singing of this piece. Her vocalization is clear and powerful, delicately expressing the emotions of the song through her ornamentation. Notably, she skillfully employs the characteristics of the Menari style, executing the melody with flexibility and capturing the audience's attention through the emphasis on each syllable. With a rich vocal range, she maintains a stable pitch across various sections of the piece, managing her breath to convey both tension and ease simultaneously. Riding naturally on the rhythm of Jungmori, Kim Min-ji adeptly varies her voice in accordance with the rhythm, further highlighting the charm of the piece. Her breath culminates the song, contributing to the overall genre's completeness.

캡션(영어): Mulletaeryeong is a labor song traditionally sung while cutting thread, which has evolved into a popular folk song of the Namdo region, originating from local songs that alleviated the tedium of labor. This piece expresses the repetitive actions and emotions of spinning through the unique musical idiom characteristic of Namdo, and it belongs to the genre of folk music within the realm of traditional music. The voice of the female vocalist Lee Joo-eun is a key element that drives this piece forward, as she seamlessly connects the flow of the song through traditional singing techniques. Lee Joo-eun maintains a stable vocal range while appropriately employing ornamentation to convey the song's emotions. Her vocal volume is adjusted to fit the structure of the piece, and her breathing flows naturally, providing a consistent sense of rhythm throughout the entire composition. Riding on the rhythm of the Jungmori jangdan, Lee Joo-eun navigates a groovy flow, skillfully managing her breath at the end of each phrase to embellish the conclusion of the piece and enhance the overall genre's completeness.

캡션(영어): Kkaturi Taryeong is a type of folk music that belongs to the Namdo Jabka and popular folk song traditions, characterized by its lively singing about the theme of going out to hunt Kkaturi, performed in a Jajinmori Jangdan. This piece effectively showcases the features of Namdo Minyo, with the vocalist's voice playing a crucial role in conveying the urgency and excitement of the hunt within the fast tempo. The voice of female vocalist Lee Joo-eun leads the energy of the piece with a solid timbre, and her vocalization is stable and clear, effectively communicating the theme to the audience. When expressing the melody, Lee Joo-eun appropriately utilizes sigimsae to evoke the emotions of traditional folk music, and her vocal strength is both powerful and well-balanced, harmonizing well with the rhythm of the piece. Her breath control seamlessly maintains the flow of the music, contributing to the heightened emotions over the brisk rhythm of Jajinmori. Lee Joo-eun's voice remains stable even amidst the rapid tempo, and in the conclusion of the piece, her breath control plays a significant role in sustaining tension and enhancing the genre's overall completeness.

캡션(한국어): 개고리타령은 남도 잡가의 일종으로, 경기민요 개고리타령과는 다른 곡이며 개구리와의 연관성도 없다. 이 곡은 남도민요의 특성을 잘 보여주는 민속악의 한 형태로, 육자배기토리와 중중모리장단으로 구성되어 있다. 다양한 사설이 섞여 부르는 이 곡은 남도 특유의 구성지고 멋스러운 소리가 돋보인다. 여창 가창자 염경애의 목소리는 이 곡의 매력을 한층 더해준다. 그녀는 발성과 시김새를 통해 전통적인 창법을 잘 살리며, 각 음을 명확하게 표현하여 곡의 흐름을 자연스럽게 이끌어간다. 염경애는 성량을 조절하며 곡의 각 부분에 적절한 긴장감을 부여하고, 호흡을 통해 멜로디의 리듬을 잘 타며 곡의 감정선을 전달한다. 중중모리의 리듬 위에서 그녀의 목소리는 유연하게 흐르며, 호흡의 조절로 곡의 마무리를 장식하고 장르적 완성도를 높인다. 이처럼 염경애의 가창은 개고리타령이 가진 전통적 가치를 더욱 빛나게 한다.
캡션(영어): Gaegoritarang is a type of Namdo folk song, distinct from the Gyeonggi folk song of the same name, and bears no connection to frogs. This piece exemplifies the characteristics of Namdo folk music and is structured in the Yukjabaegi-tori and Jungjungmori jangdan. The song, which incorporates various lyrics, showcases the unique and elegant sound typical of Namdo. The voice of the female vocalist, Yeom Gyeong-ae, further enhances the charm of this piece. She skillfully preserves traditional singing techniques through her vocalization and ornamentation, clearly articulating each note to guide the flow of the song naturally. Yeom Gyeong-ae adjusts her vocal volume to impart appropriate tension to each section of the piece, effectively conveying the emotional line of the melody through her breath control. Her voice flows gracefully over the Jungjungmori rhythm, and her management of breath beautifully concludes the piece, elevating its genre-specific completeness. In this way, Yeom Gyeong-ae's singing shines a brighter light on the traditional value inherent in Gaegoritarang.

캡션(영어): Jindo Arirang is a representative Arirang based on the Namdo Yukjabaegi style, belonging to the genre of folk music. This piece features the refrain "Ariari Arirang, Suri Suri Arirang," sung in accordance with the Semachi Jangdan, expressing both joy and sorrow, and it is widely loved for the enjoyment of improvising lyrics. The voice of female vocalist Yeom Gyeong-ae beautifully captures the essence of this piece, as she leads the emotional expression through traditional singing techniques. Yeom Gyeong-ae skillfully navigates between high and low notes with her vocalization, utilizing shigimsae appropriately to enrich the rhythm and melody of the piece. Her vocal volume is adjusted according to the flow of the song, captivating the audience with variations in intensity. Breath control also plays a crucial role, maintaining tension through appropriate breathing as the piece unfolds, while providing a sense of ease in the concluding section to enhance the overall quality of the performance. Riding the rhythms of Semachi and Jungmori, Yeom Gyeong-ae naturally flows with the music, her breath embellishing the conclusion of the piece and further highlighting the distinctive characteristics of the genre.

캡션(영어): Boryeom is a song sung at the beginning of Namdo Jabka, a form of folk music that expresses wishes for the peace and well-being of the nation, based on Buddhist prayers. This piece distinctly showcases the characteristics of Namdo Minyo, starting with a solemn and dignified atmosphere and gradually building in intensity within its musical structure. The voice of the female vocalist, Yeom Gyeong-ae, serves as a crucial element guiding the progression of the piece; she conveys deep emotions through her vocalization and delicately adjusts the nuances, effectively expressing the charm of traditional folk songs. Her vocal range adapts appropriately to the development of the piece, and through controlled breathing, she seamlessly connects the flow of the melody. Over the rhythm of Jungmori, the vocalist rides the rhythm of the song, clearly distinguishing each phrase with a relaxed breath, and at the conclusion of the piece, she utilizes her breath to leave a lingering resonance, enhancing the genre's completeness. In this way, Yeom Gyeong-ae's singing style faithfully reflects the structure of the piece while well inheriting the tradition of Namdo Minyo.

캡션(영어): Yukjabaegi is a representative folk song and narrative song from the Namdo region, encapsulating the joys and sorrows of life within the rich melodies of Yukjabaegi-tori. This piece begins with a slow Jinyangjo jangdan, characterized by a deep expression of sorrow, and belongs to the genre of folk music, specifically the minyo, where one can truly experience the essence of Namdo sound. The voice of female vocalist Jo Jeong-hee serves as a crucial element in guiding this piece. Through her vocalization and stylistic nuances, she conveys the emotions and meanings of the song, faithfully adhering to the traditional singing style of Namdo folk songs while also adding her personal interpretation. Jo Jeong-hee skillfully adjusts her vocal volume to flow smoothly with the slow rhythm of the Jinyangjo, elongating each note while managing her breath to maintain both tension and stability. Her stylistic nuances enhance the traditional elements while deepening the emotional expression, enriching the narrative of the piece. Over the rhythm of Jinyang, Jo Jeong-hee harmonizes her breath to beautifully conclude the song, and this control of breath contributes to the overall completeness of the piece. Overall, Jo Jeong-hee's voice plays a significant role in preserving the traditional characteristics of Yukjabaegi while infusing it with her unique interpretation.

This piece effectively showcases the characteristics of Namdo folk songs, progressing in a brisk 3/4 time signature known as Semachi, while the melodic features are similar to those of Yukjabaegi. The voice of the female vocalist Jo Jeong-hee is a crucial element that guides the flow of the piece; she maintains a stable vocal range in her delivery and expresses traditional emotions through her use of vocal ornamentation, or sigimsae. Jo Jeong-hee flexibly conveys the melody in accordance with the song's structure, employing a singing technique that imbues each syllable with emotion. Her vocal volume is appropriately adjusted throughout the development of the piece, and her breath control aids in smoothly connecting longer phrases. Notably, over the rhythm of Jinyang, Jo Jeong-hee's voice naturally rides the flow of the song, and her breath plays a vital role in enhancing the overall completeness of the piece during its concluding sections. These elements collectively illustrate the beauty inherent in Jajin Yukjabaegi as a traditional folk music form.

캡션(한국어): 흥타령은 남도 잡가의 대표적인 곡으로, 경기민요와는 구별되는 남도민요의 특징을 잘 드러낸다. 이 곡은 인생의 무상함과 애절한 감정을 중모리장단에 담아 노래하며, 후렴구인 '아이고 데고 허허 성화가 났네'는 깊은 탄식과 한을 자아낸다. 여창 가창자 염경애의 목소리는 이 곡의 감정을 이끌어가는 중요한 요소로 작용한다. 그녀는 발성에서 안정적인 음역대를 유지하며, 시김새를 적절히 사용하여 곡의 감정을 표현한다. 특히 중모리장단에 맞춰서 리듬의 흐름을 잘 타며, 멜로디를 유연하게 구사한다. 염경애는 성량을 조절하여 각 구절의 강조점을 잘 살리며, 호흡을 통해 곡의 긴장감을 조절한다. 이러한 호흡은 곡의 전개에서 자연스럽게 이어지며, 중모리의 리듬 위에서 그녀의 목소리가 유기적으로 연결된다. 곡의 마무리에서는 호흡을 통해 여운을 남기며, 장르적 완성도를 높이는 데 기여한다.
캡션(영어): Heungtaryeong is a representative piece of Namdo folk song, distinctly showcasing the characteristics of Namdo minyo, which can be differentiated from Gyeonggi minyo. This song encapsulates the transience of life and poignant emotions within the medium tempo Jangdan, with the refrain "Aigo dego heoheo seonghwa ga natne" evoking deep sighs and a sense of sorrow. The voice of the female vocalist, Yeom Gyeong-ae, serves as a crucial element in conveying the emotions of the piece. She maintains a stable vocal range in her singing, appropriately utilizing vocal embellishments to express the song's sentiments. Particularly, she adeptly follows the rhythmic flow aligned with the medium tempo Jangdan, executing the melody with flexibility. Yeom Gyeong-ae skillfully adjusts her vocal volume to highlight the emphasis of each phrase, while her breath control modulates the tension of the song. This breathing is seamlessly integrated into the development of the piece, allowing her voice to connect organically over the rhythm of the medium tempo. In the conclusion of the song, her breath leaves a lingering resonance, contributing to the overall artistic completeness of the genre.

캡션(영어): Bangataeryeong is a type of folk music incorporated into the 'Sim Bongsa Hwangseong Olraganeun Daemok' section of the pansori piece Simcheongga, originally a folk song that has been adapted into pansori. This piece distinctly showcases the characteristics of Namdo minyo and encapsulates the essence of traditional folk culture. Female vocalist Yeom Gyeong-ae leads the piece with her unique singing style, conveying the imagery of pounding rice and the emotions involved in the process through her vocalization and embellishments. Her voice maintains a clear distinction of syllables and a rhythmic flow throughout the various sections of the performance, effectively utilizing embellishments to emphasize the traditional elements of the piece. Yeom Gyeong-ae skillfully manages her vocal power while sustaining the tension of the song, seamlessly connecting the flow of the melody through her breath control. Over the rhythm of jungjungmori, she adeptly grasps the structure of the piece, introducing flexible variations in accordance with the rhythm, thus captivating the listeners. In the conclusion of the piece, she appropriately regulates her breath to leave a lingering resonance, enhancing the overall quality of traditional folk music.

캡션(한국어): 방아타령2는 민속악의 한 갈래인 남도민요로, 판소리 심청가 중 '심봉사 황성 올라가는 대목'에 삽입된 전통적인 곡이다. 이 곡은 본래 민요였던 방아타령이 판소리의 요소를 차용하여 발전한 형태로, 고대 중국의 설화를 배경으로 한 내용이 담겨 있으며 방아의 종류와 찧는 모습을 노래하고 있다. 여창 가창자 염경애는 이 곡을 통해 전통적인 창법을 바탕으로 목소리를 이끌어간다. 그녀의 발성은 안정적이며, 시김새를 적절히 구사하여 전통적인 민요의 특성을 잘 살리고 있다. 특히, 염경애는 멜로디를 표현하는 데 있어 각 음절의 발음을 명확히 하며, 감정을 담아내기 위해 호흡의 길이를 조절하는 기술을 보여준다. 자진모리 장단의 리듬 위에서 그녀는 경쾌한 흐름을 유지하며, 곡의 전개에 따라 적절한 성량으로 변화를 주어 청중의 귀를 사로잡는다. 곡의 마무리에서는 호흡을 통해 자연스럽게 여운을 남기며, 전체적인 장르적 완성도를 높인다. 이러한 요소들이 모여 방아타령2는 전통적인 남도민요의 매력을 잘 드러내는 곡으로 자리 잡고 있다.
캡션(영어): Bang'ataryeong 2 is a traditional piece embedded within the pansori narrative of "Simcheongga," specifically in the section titled 'Sim Bongsa Ascending to Hwangseong,' and it belongs to the genre of Namdo minyo, a branch of folk music. This piece is an evolved form of the original folk song Bang'ataryeong, which incorporates elements of pansori and is based on ancient Chinese folklore, depicting the types of pestles and the act of pounding. The female vocalist Yeom Gyeong-ae leads the performance with a traditional singing style, showcasing a stable vocal production and skillfully employing various ornamentations to highlight the characteristics of traditional folk music. Notably, Yeom Gyeong-ae articulates each syllable clearly while demonstrating the technique of adjusting breath length to convey emotion effectively. Over the rhythm of the jazinmori jangdan, she maintains a lively flow and varies her vocal intensity appropriately throughout the progression of the piece, captivating the audience. In the conclusion of the song, she leaves a lingering resonance through her breath, enhancing the overall genre's completeness. These elements collectively establish Bang'ataryeong 2 as a piece that well exemplifies the charm of traditional Namdo minyo.

캡션(영어): Iyahungtaryeong is a native folk song from Jeju Island, originating from a labor song sung while weaving a manggeon (traditional headgear). It celebrates the scenic beauty of Jeju and, while influenced by mainland musical styles, retains the unique emotional essence of Jeju, resulting in a lively yet rich flavor characteristic of the folk music genre. The voice of the female vocalist, Cheon Jumi, plays a crucial role in the development of this piece, showcasing clarity in the high notes and stability in the low tones. Cheon Jumi maintains traditional singing techniques while skillfully employing nuances that highlight the distinctive qualities of Jeju folk songs. Her vocal range is balanced throughout the piece, and her breath control serves as an essential element in seamlessly connecting long phrases. Riding the rhythm of the semachi jangdan, Cheon Jumi flows gracefully, infusing each syllable with vitality. Her breath contributes to the conclusion of the piece, playing a significant role in the modern reinterpretation of traditional elements of Jeju folk music. The combination of these elements culminates in Iyahungtaryeong, a piece that maximizes the charm of Jeju folk songs.

캡션(영어): Neoyeongnayoung is a popular folk song from Jeju, meaning "You and I," which revolves around the theme of love between men and women and is joyfully sung to the rhythm of Ggutgeori Jangdan. 캡션(영어): This piece is a folk song from Jeju Island that sings of the scenic beauty of Hallasan Mountain and Seogwipo, and it is also known by the name 'Odolttogi.' Starting with the refrain 'Dungrye Dangsil,' this song conveys a very bright and cheerful feeling, and it is sung in a call-and-response manner to the slow Gukgeori Jangdan. The voice of the female vocalist Lee Joo-eun is a crucial element that guides the flow of the piece, as she effectively embodies the characteristics of Jeju folk music through traditional singing techniques. Lee Joo-eun clearly expresses the melody of the song through her vocalization, appropriately employing vocal embellishments to convey the unique emotions of the folk song. Her vocal range flexibly adapts to the rhythm of the piece, while her breathing remains stable, seamlessly integrating into the progression of the song. Riding the rhythm of the Gukgeori Jangdan, Lee Joo-eun adjusts her breath at the beginning and end of each phrase, elegantly concluding the piece. This harmonious control of breath contributes to the genre's overall completeness in Jeju folk music.

The voice of the female vocalist Lee Joo-eun serves as a central element that drives the song, as her vocalization faithfully adheres to traditional singing techniques while clearly articulating each syllable. The ornamentation reflects the emotional essence of Jeju folk music, and her vocal range flexibly varies with the flow of the piece, allowing listeners to experience a sense of immersion. The breathing aligns naturally with the progression of the song, and during longer phrases, she skillfully manages her breath to maintain stable pronunciation. This flow of breath enhances the rhythmic quality of the piece, contributing to the overall completeness of the genre, while in the end, Lee Joo-eun's breath gently concludes the song, leaving a lingering resonance with the audience.

캡션(한국어): 강강술래 1은 남도민요의 전통을 잘 담고 있는 민속악 곡으로, 강강술래의 독특한 구성과 창법이 돋보인다. 이 곡은 미-mi, 라-la, 시-si, 도-do′의 음을 기반으로 하며, 미를 길게 소리 내는 방식과 도-si의 꺾는 표현이 특징적이다. 여창 가창자 조정희는 이 곡에서 미를 강조하며 길게 소리 내어 청중의 귀를 사로잡는다. 그녀의 목소리는 각 음을 정확하게 표현하며, 특히 시김새의 사용이 두드러진다. 느린 템포에서 잔가락이 풍부하게 들어가며, 시김새의 변화가 곡의 감정을 더욱 풍부하게 만든다. 중모리의 장단 위에서 조정희는 리드미컬하게 흐름을 타며, 각 음의 길이와 강약을 조절하여 곡의 진행에 맞춰 자연스럽게 호흡을 이어간다. 그녀의 호흡은 곡의 마무리를 부드럽게 장식하며, 전통 민속악의 완성도를 높이는 데 기여한다.
캡션(영어): Ganggangsullae 1 is a folk music piece that beautifully encapsulates the tradition of Namdo Minyo, showcasing the unique structure and vocal techniques characteristic of Ganggangsullae. This piece is based on the notes mi-mi, la-la, si-si, and do-do′, with a distinctive emphasis on the elongated pronunciation of mi and the expressive ornamentation of do-si. The female vocalist Jo Jeong-hee emphasizes mi in this piece, drawing out the sound to captivate the audience's ears. Her voice articulates each note with precision, particularly highlighting the use of sigimsae (ornamentation). The slow tempo allows for rich embellishments, and the variations in sigimsae further enhance the emotional depth of the piece. Over the jangdan of jungmori, Jo Jeong-hee flows rhythmically, adjusting the length and dynamics of each note to seamlessly maintain the natural breath of the progression. Her breath gently adorns the conclusion of the piece, contributing to the overall refinement of traditional folk music.

캡션(한국어): 골패타령은 남도민요의 특성을 잘 드러내는 민속악의 일종으로, 골패 놀이의 용어와 상황을 가사에 담아 부르는 곡이다. 이 곡은 자진모리장단에 맞춰 흥겹고 멋스럽게 노래하며, 놀이판의 흥분과 긴장감을 음악적으로 표현한 재치 있는 민요로, 전통적인 남도의 정서를 잘 담고 있다. 여창 가창자 천주미의 목소리는 이 곡을 이끌어가는 중요한 요소로 작용하며, 그녀의 발성은 곡의 리드미컬한 흐름을 잘 살린다. 천주미는 고유의 창법을 통해 멜로디를 유연하게 표현하며, 시김새를 적절히 활용하여 가사의 의미를 생동감 있게 전달한다. 그녀의 성량은 곡의 다이나믹을 조절하며, 호흡의 조절을 통해 긴 구절을 안정적으로 이어간다. 자진모리의 경쾌한 리듬 위에서 천주미는 곡의 흐름을 타며, 각 구절마다 적절한 호흡을 통해 자연스럽게 마무리 짓고, 이는 전반적인 장르적 완성도를 높이는 데 기여한다. 이러한 요소들이 결합되어 골패타령은 단순한 민요 이상의 의미를 지니며, 청중에게 깊은 인상을 남긴다.
캡션(영어): Golpae Taryeong is a type of folk music that vividly showcases the characteristics of Namdo Minyo, incorporating the terminology and situations of the Golpae game into its lyrics. This song is performed in a lively and stylish manner, set to the Jajinmori Jangdan, and cleverly expresses the excitement and tension of the game through music, encapsulating the traditional emotions of the southern region of Korea. The voice of the female vocalist, Cheon Jumi, serves as a crucial element that guides the piece, with her vocalization effectively enhancing the rhythmic flow of the song. Cheon Jumi flexibly interprets the melody through her unique singing style and employs appropriate vocal embellishments to convey the meaning of the lyrics vividly. Her vocal power adjusts the dynamics of the piece, and through careful breath control, she maintains stability across long phrases. Riding on the brisk rhythm of the Jajinmori, Cheon Jumi naturally concludes each verse with suitable breaths, contributing to the overall artistic completeness of the genre. These combined elements elevate Golpae Taryeong beyond a mere folk song, leaving a profound impression on the audience.

캡션(한국어): 눈사람은 여성국극 '못잊어'의 서곡으로 사용된 남도 신민요로, 눈 오는 날의 풍경을 엇모리장단에 담아 불린다. 이 곡은 서정적인 가사와 독특한 리듬이 어우러져 환상적인 분위기를 자아내며, 남도민요의 특징이 잘 드러나는 민속악 > 민요 장르에 속한다. 여창 가창자 이주은의 목소리는 곡의 전개에서 중요한 역할을 하며, 다이내믹한 표현력으로 청중을 끌어당긴다. 그녀의 단단한 음색은 곡의 서정성을 더욱 강조하며, 멜로디를 표현하는 방식에서 시김새와 성량의 조화를 통해 감정의 깊이를 더한다. 이주은은 호흡을 조절하며 곡의 흐름을 매끄럽게 이어가고, 강약 조절을 통해 청중에게 강한 인상을 남긴다. 중중모리의 리듬 위에서 그녀의 목소리는 자연스럽게 흐름을 타며, 호흡의 리듬감이 곡의 마무리를 장식하고 장르적 완성도를 높인다. 이주은의 창법은 곡이 전하는 감성을 더욱 풍부하게 만들어, 남도민요의 매력을 잘 전달한다.
캡션(영어): ‘Nunsaram’ is a Namdo folk song used as the overture for the women's gukgeuk 'Motijuh,' capturing the scenery of a snowy day through the rhythmic pattern of Eotmori Jangdan. This piece combines lyrical lyrics with a unique rhythm, creating a fantastical atmosphere and exemplifying the characteristics of Namdo minyo, belonging to the folk music genre of minyo. The voice of female vocalist Lee Joo-eun plays a crucial role in the development of the piece, drawing the audience in with her dynamic expressiveness. Her solid timbre further emphasizes the lyrical quality of the song, and her interpretation of the melody enhances the emotional depth through the harmony of ornamentation and vocal power. Lee Joo-eun skillfully manages her breath to maintain a smooth flow throughout the piece, and her control of dynamics leaves a strong impression on the audience. Over the rhythm of Jungjungmori, her voice flows naturally, with the rhythmic quality of her breathing adorning the conclusion of the piece and elevating its genre-specific completeness. Lee Joo-eun's singing style enriches the emotions conveyed by the song, effectively communicating the charm of Namdo minyo.

캡션(한국어): 꽃타령은 박헌봉이 작사하고 박귀희가 작곡한 신민요로, 남도민요의 특징을 잘 드러내는 민속악의 한 예이다. 이 곡은 여러 가지 꽃을 주제로 하여 봄날의 화사함과 꽃의 아름다움을 표현하는 경쾌한 선율로 구성되어 있다. 여창 가창자 이주은의 목소리는 이 곡의 중심에서 중요한 역할을 하며, 그녀의 발성은 맑고 청아한 음색을 통해 꽃의 아름다움을 전달한다. 이주은은 곡의 멜로디를 표현하는 과정에서 시김새를 적절히 활용하여 전통적인 민요의 맛을 살리고 있으며, 성량이 풍부하여 곡의 다양한 구성을 효과적으로 소화한다. 그녀의 호흡은 곡의 리듬에 잘 맞춰져 있으며, 자진모리의 경쾌한 리듬 위에서 자연스럽게 흐름을 타고 있다. 이주은의 호흡은 곡의 마무리를 장식하며, 전체적인 장르의 완성도를 높이는 데 기여한다.
캡션(영어): Flower Song is a new folk song with lyrics by Park Heon-bong and music composed by Park Gwi-hee, exemplifying the characteristics of Namdo folk music. This piece is composed of lively melodies that express the brightness of spring days and the beauty of flowers, centered around various floral themes. The voice of the female vocalist Lee Joo-eun plays a crucial role at the heart of the piece, as her vocalization conveys the beauty of flowers through a clear and pure timbre. In the process of expressing the melody, Lee Joo-eun effectively utilizes vocal embellishments to preserve the essence of traditional folk songs, and her rich vocal range allows her to navigate the diverse structures of the piece effectively. Her breath control aligns well with the rhythm of the song, flowing naturally over the brisk tempo of the Jajinmori rhythm. Lee Joo-eun's breath enhances the conclusion of the piece, contributing to the overall completeness of the genre.

캡션(영어): Dungataeryeong is a Nambo folk song and a new folk song that begins with "Namwonsanseong," showcasing the characteristics of Nambo minyo, a branch of traditional folk music. This piece is transmitted with an upbeat melody accompanied by the refrain "dungadunga," and it appears to have originated from sounds sung to soothe children or to elevate the mood. The voice of female vocalist Jo Jeong-hee naturally guides the flow of the piece, and her singing style faithfully reflects the elements of traditional folk songs. Jo Jeong-hee clearly conveys the melody through her vocalization, effectively utilizing vocal embellishments to enhance the emotional depth. Her vocal range fluidly changes according to the development of the piece, and her excellent breath control maintains a stable rhythm throughout. Over the rhythm of jungjungmori, Jo Jeong-hee maintains a steady beat, adjusting the length and emphasis of each syllable to ensure a smooth continuity of the song. Her breathing adorns the conclusion of the piece, contributing to the overall completeness of the traditional folk song.

캡션(영어): Nulttugi 1 is a form of traditional folk music sung around the Lunar New Year, showcasing the distinctive characteristics of Namdo minyo. This piece captures the dynamism of the Nulttugi game within its lively jangdan, enhancing the festive atmosphere of the holiday. The voice of the female vocalist Jo Jeong-hee smoothly guides the flow of the piece, expressing the melody through stable vocalization in accordance with the mid-mori jangdan. Jo Jeong-hee effectively employs nuances to preserve the essence of traditional folk songs, adjusting her vocal range to convey the appropriate pitch for each phrase. Her breath harmonizes well with the rhythm of the piece, naturally flowing over the foundation of mid-mori while simultaneously providing a sense of tension and stability. These elements come together in harmony, elevating the overall quality of the piece and further highlighting the charm of traditional folk music.

캡션(영어): Nongbuga is a folk song from the Jeolla region, originally derived from the rice planting sounds known as Sangsa-sori, which was incorporated into the pansori piece Chunhyangga before evolving into an independent popular folk song of the Namdo region. This piece exemplifies the characteristics of folk music well. The voice of female vocalist Jo Jeong-hee plays a crucial role in the development of this song, as she fluidly navigates between the long notes of the Jungmori jangdan and the brisk, lively notes of the Jajin sori, expressing the melody with great artistry. Jo Jeong-hee delivers each note clearly through her vocalization, skillfully employing stylistic nuances to preserve the traditional elements of the folk song while captivating the audience with variations in her singing technique. Her vocal range guides the flow of the piece, maintaining a sense of ease in the long notes while exuding even more dynamic energy in the lively sections. Over the rhythm of the Jungmori, Jo Jeong-hee naturally rides the flow, and the arrangement of her breath enhances the conclusion of the piece, elevating the overall genre's completeness. In this way, Jo Jeong-hee's voice beautifully embodies the folk characteristics of Nongbuga, radiating a charm that transcends the boundaries between tradition and modernity.

The female vocalist Jo Jeong-hee serves as the protagonist of this piece, and her voice is a crucial element that guides the flow of the song. Jo Jeong-hee expresses the melodic structure of Yukjabaegi tori naturally, based on a solid foundation of vocalization, while appropriately employing sigimsae to evoke the emotions of traditional folk songs. She organically connects the long notes and the rapid passages, adjusting her vocal volume to maximize the expressiveness of each phrase. Breath control is also vital; Jo Jeong-hee maintains stable breathing in accordance with the rhythm of Jungjungmori, regulating the tension of the piece. This harmony of breath and rhythm contributes to the overall completeness of the song, leaving a profound impression on the audience.

캡션(영어): Dalmaji is a seasonal folk song sung during the ritual of burning the moon house on the first full moon of the lunar year, embodying wishes for a bountiful harvest and the warding off of misfortune. This piece reflects the earnest hopes for the well-being and prosperity of the village community, showcasing the characteristics of folk music from the Namdo region. The voice of female vocalist Jo Jeong-hee leads the development of the song, and her singing style faithfully reflects the features of traditional folk songs. Through her vocalization, Jo Jeong-hee clearly expresses the melody of the piece, effectively conveying the emotions of the song with appropriate use of vocal embellishments. Her stable vocal power and excellent breath control naturally guide the flow of the piece. Over the rhythm of the Jungmori jangdan, her voice moves flexibly, effectively enhancing the structure of the song in accordance with the rhythm. At the conclusion of the piece, Jo Jeong-hee leaves a lingering resonance through her breath, contributing to the overall completeness of the traditional folk song.

캡션(영어): Dongbaek Taryeong is a Namdo folk song composed by the master Han Il-seop in 1961, encapsulating the beauty of the camellia flower and the excitement of a lover within the melodic framework of Namdo gye-myeonjo. This piece serves as a form of folk music that effectively showcases the lyrical and structured charm of Namdo sound, with distinct characteristics of Namdo minyo clearly evident. The female vocalist Jo Jeong-hee plays a crucial role in the performance of this song, as her voice conveys the emotional essence of traditional Namdo minyo. Through her vocalization and nuanced ornamentation, she expresses the melody while infusing deep emotion into each syllable, guiding the flow of the piece. Her vocal range is stable, and her breath control is exceptional, allowing for flexible variations in accordance with the progression of the song. Riding on the rhythm of Jungmori, the vocalist navigates the rhythmic flow, skillfully employing breath at the end of each phrase to embellish the conclusion of the piece, and this control of breath contributes to the genre's overall completeness. Jo Jeong-hee's voice transcends mere melody delivery, profoundly expressing the tradition and sentiment of Namdo minyo, playing a significant role in conveying the meaning of the song to the audience.

캡션(영어): Donghaebada is a new folk song composed and written by Han Il-seop, capturing the lonely feelings of waiting for a departed lover. This piece paradoxically expresses the Korean sentiment of overcoming sorrow with joy by setting its melancholic lyrics to an upbeat Dongsalpuri Jangdan. The characteristics of Namdo Minyo are prominently showcased in this song, conveying deep emotions within the context of traditional folk music. The voice of female vocalist Jo Jeong-hee plays a crucial role in guiding the emotional line of the piece. She maintains a soft timbre in her vocalization and delicately expresses the song's emotions through her use of sigimsae. Jo Jeong-hee skillfully adjusts her breath for each syllable, ensuring a smooth flow of the melody while emphasizing the climax of the piece through her vocal power. Her singing technique preserves the traditional methods of Namdo Minyo while also adding a modern interpretation. Over the Hwimori Jangdan, Jo Jeong-hee naturally rides the changes in rhythm, singing in a way that harmonizes with the song's rhythmic feel. Her breath plays an important role in the conclusion of the piece, contributing to the overall completeness of the performance. These elements further highlight the traditional charm of Donghaebada.

캡션(한국어): 둥당애타령은 전남 도서 지역의 향토민요로, '둥당애'라는 구음 후렴구가 특징인 민속악 중에서도 남도민요의 전형적인 예시를 보여준다. 이 곡은 여성들이 유희요나 노동요로 부르며 물장구 등을 치며 놀 때 함께 즐기던 흥겨운 노래로, 지역의 문화와 정서를 고스란히 담고 있다. 여창 가창자 염경애의 목소리는 곡의 분위기를 이끌어가는 데 중요한 역할을 한다. 그녀의 창법은 전통적인 민요의 특징을 잘 반영하며, 발성과 시김새를 통해 곡의 감정을 효과적으로 전달한다. 염경애는 중중모리의 리듬을 타고 자연스럽게 멜로디를 표현하며, 곡의 흐름을 부드럽게 이어간다. 그녀의 성량은 곡의 각 구절을 강조하며, 호흡 조절을 통해 긴장감과 여유를 적절히 조화시킨다. 중중모리의 리듬 위에서 염경애의 목소리는 곡의 전체적인 완성도를 높이며, 호흡의 마무리가 자연스럽고 여운이 남도록 장식한다. 이러한 요소들은 둥당애타령이 가진 향토적인 매력을 더욱 돋보이게 한다.
캡션(영어): Dungdang-ae Taryeong is a local folk song from the Jeonnam coastal region, characterized by the refrain 'Dungdang-ae,' which exemplifies the typical features of Namdo folk songs. This piece is a lively song traditionally sung by women during leisure or labor, often accompanied by hand clapping, reflecting the culture and emotions of the area. The voice of female vocalist Yeom Gyeong-ae plays a crucial role in shaping the atmosphere of the song. Her singing style effectively mirrors the characteristics of traditional folk music, conveying the song's emotions through her vocalization and ornamentation. Yeom Gyeong-ae naturally expresses the melody while riding the rhythm of Jungjungmori, smoothly connecting the flow of the piece. Her vocal strength emphasizes each phrase, skillfully balancing tension and relaxation through breath control. On the rhythm of Jungjungmori, Yeom Gyeong-ae's voice enhances the overall completeness of the song, with her breath concluding naturally and leaving a lingering resonance. These elements further highlight the local charm inherent in Dungdang-ae Taryeong.

This piece joyfully expresses the labor of picking mulberry leaves and the love between men and women, capturing a bright and cheerful atmosphere that has garnered widespread popularity. The voice of female vocalist Lee Joo-eun serves as the centerpiece of the song, with her vocalization effectively conveying the song's liveliness. When expressing the melody, Lee Joo-eun navigates freely between high and low notes, guiding the flow of the piece naturally. Her embellishments enhance the traditional characteristics of folk songs while adding a modern sensibility, amplifying the song's charm. The volume is appropriately controlled, leaving a profound impression on listeners as it harmonizes with the rhythm of each phrase. Her breath is distributed suitably according to the rhythm of the piece, allowing her voice to flow flexibly in alignment with the development of the song while riding the rhythm of the Jungmori jangdan. Lee Joo-eun's breathing plays a particularly crucial role in the concluding section of the piece, contributing to the overall completeness. Over the rhythm of Jungmori, her voice flows with stability, concluding the song in a manner that leaves a lingering resonance with the audience.

Lee Joo-eun expresses the melody with clear intonation and appropriately employs vocal embellishments, effectively capturing the characteristics of traditional folk songs. Her vocal range harmonizes well with the dynamism of the piece, and her breath control is natural and fluid, further accentuating the rhythmic quality of the music. Lee Joo-eun's breathing also plays a crucial role in the conclusion of the piece, leaving a profound resonance with the audience and contributing to the overall artistic completeness of the genre.

The female vocalist Lee Joo-eun plays a leading role in this piece, guiding the flow of the song. Her voice expresses the melody smoothly and flexibly, employing traditional singing techniques to appropriately incorporate embellishments that convey emotion. Her vocalization is stable, clearly articulating each note while fluidly adapting to the rhythm of the piece. Lee Joo-eun skillfully manages her breath to sustain long phrases, seamlessly blending into the rhythm of jeongjeongmori, capturing the audience's attention and introducing dynamic changes as the song progresses. Her breath culminates in the conclusion of the piece, contributing to the overall genre's completeness. In this way, Lee Joo-eun's voice plays a crucial role in maintaining the traditional elements of Kwaejinachinchingnane while smoothly connecting the flow of the song.

캡션(한국어): 함양양잠가는 남도민요에 속하는 민속악으로, 경남 함양 지방에서 뽕을 따고 누에를 치며 부르던 노동요에서 유래한 곡이다. 이 노래는 양잠을 통해 의생활과 부모 봉양을 책임지던 서민들의 삶과 애환을 담고 있으며, "에야 듸야", "두둥가" 등의 후렴구로 일의 고됨을 잊고 흥을 돋우는 특징이 있다. 여창 가창자 이주은의 목소리는 이 곡을 이끌어가는 중요한 요소로, 그녀는 발성을 통해 곡의 감정을 전달하며 시김새를 적절히 활용하여 전통적인 민요의 매력을 잘 살린다. 이주은은 고음과 저음을 자유롭게 넘나들며 멜로디를 표현하고, 각 음절에 정성을 담아 부드러운 흐름을 유지한다. 그녀의 성량은 곡의 전개에 따라 변화하며, 호흡의 조절이 뛰어나 긴 구절에서도 안정감을 잃지 않는다. 중중모리의 리듬 위에서 이주은은 리듬을 타며 자연스럽게 곡의 흐름을 이어가고, 그녀의 호흡은 곡의 마무리를 부드럽게 장식하며 전통 민요의 완성도를 높인다.
캡션(영어): Hamyang Yangjam is a folk song belonging to the Namdo Minyo genre, originating from labor songs sung while picking mulberries and raising silkworms in the Hamyang region of Gyeongnam. This song encapsulates the lives and sorrows of common people who were responsible for their livelihoods and caring for their parents through sericulture, featuring refrains such as 'Eya Dwiya' and 'Dudungga' that help to alleviate the hardships of work and uplift the spirit. The voice of female vocalist Lee Joo-eun is a crucial element in leading this piece, as she conveys the emotions of the song through her vocalization and skillfully employs traditional ornamentation to enhance the charm of the folk song. Lee Joo-eun fluidly navigates between high and low notes to express the melody, infusing each syllable with care to maintain a smooth flow. Her vocal power varies according to the progression of the song, demonstrating excellent breath control that ensures stability even in long phrases. Over the rhythm of Jungjungmori, Lee Joo-eun rides the rhythm naturally, seamlessly continuing the flow of the piece, and her breath gracefully adorns the conclusion of the song, elevating the completeness of the traditional folk music.

캡션(한국어): 화초사거리는 남도잡가로, 사당패 소리를 수용하여 만들어진 독특한 민속악의 일종이다. 이 곡은 입타령과 화초타령으로 구성되어 있으며, 경서도와 남도 음악 어법이 혼합되어 다채로운 음악적 색깔을 보여준다. 여창 가창자 염경애는 이 곡에서 중모리 장단에 맞춰 목소리를 통해 곡의 흐름을 이끌어간다. 그녀의 발성은 곡의 구조에 잘 맞아떨어지며, 시김새를 적절히 사용하여 전통적인 민요의 매력을 잘 살린다. 염경애는 성량을 조절하며 곡의 각 부분에서 멜로디를 명확하게 표현하고, 호흡을 통해 자연스럽고 유려한 흐름을 만들어낸다. 중모리의 리듬 위에서 가창자는 그루비한 리듬을 타며, 호흡의 조절로 곡의 마무리를 장식하고 장르적 완성도를 높인다. 전체적으로 염경애의 가창은 화초사거리의 전통적 요소를 잘 살리면서도, 곡의 감정을 효과적으로 전달하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다.
캡션(영어): Hwacho Sago is a unique form of folk music that originates from the Namdo region, created by incorporating the sounds of the Sadangpae. This piece is composed of the Ip Taryeong and Hwacho Taryeong, showcasing a rich musical color through the blending of Gyeongseodo and Namdo musical styles. The female vocalist Yeom Gyeong-ae leads the flow of the piece with her voice, adhering to the Jungmori Jangdan rhythm. Her vocalization aligns well with the structure of the piece, effectively utilizing vocal embellishments to highlight the charm of traditional folk songs. Yeom Gyeong-ae adjusts her vocal volume, clearly expressing the melody in each section, and creates a natural and fluid flow through her breath control. Over the rhythm of Jungmori, the vocalist rides a groovy rhythm, enhancing the conclusion of the piece and elevating its genre-specific completeness. Overall, Yeom Gyeong-ae's singing plays a crucial role in preserving the traditional elements of Hwacho Sago while effectively conveying the emotions of the piece.

캡션(영어): Yusangga is one of the twelve Jangga of Gyeonggi, representing a quintessential folk song that sings of the beautiful landscapes of spring. This piece features lengthy and sophisticated lyrics, showcasing the characteristics of Gyeonggi Jangga, and provides an opportunity to glimpse the skills of professional singers from the Seoul and Gyeonggi regions. The female vocalist Chae Su-hyun effectively conveys the beauty of Yusangga with her voice in this piece. She skillfully utilizes vocal techniques and embellishments to delicately express the melody of the song. Chae Su-hyun's vocal range leads the flow of the piece, adding emotion through precise pronunciation and embellishments for each syllable. Her breath control is stable, appropriately adjusted throughout each phrase to maintain a sense of rhythm. Over the Dodori (6 beats) rhythm, Chae Su-hyun flows gracefully, modulating her breath in accordance with the development of the piece, leaving a lingering resonance in the concluding section. This breath control acts as a crucial element that enhances the completeness of the piece, further highlighting the traditional charm of Gyeonggi Jangga.

The voice of female vocalist Chae Su-hyun serves as a crucial element guiding the flow of the piece. Through her vocalization, she flexibly expresses the melody in accordance with the rhythm of the song, employing appropriate sigimsae to enhance the traditional feel of the piece. Her rich vocal tone ensures that each syllable is clearly articulated, and she manages the tension through her breathing, seamlessly connecting the flow of the song. Notably, over the rhythm of the semachi jangdan, the vocalist adeptly rides the rhythmic changes while maintaining the flow, skillfully controlling her breath at the end of each phrase to embellish the conclusion of the piece. This breath control elevates the overall quality of the song and further accentuates the characteristics of traditional Gyeonggi Jangga.

The voice of the female vocalist Kim Se-yoon serves as a crucial element in guiding the piece, as she conveys the emotions of the song through her vocal techniques and expressive nuances. Notably, her pronunciation in the introduction evokes a sense of lamentation, while in the middle section, she fluidly expresses the melody with a lively rhythm. She skillfully adjusts her vocal volume and employs breath control that aligns with each phrase, allowing for a natural progression of the piece. Over the rhythm of the Doduri Jangdan, Kim Se-yoon effectively communicates the structure of the song with her voice, and her breath control adorns the conclusion of the piece. These elements contribute to enhancing the genre's overall completeness in Gyeonggi Jabka.

This piece distinguishes sections of the lyrics through the refrain "Nolgo gase," expressing the sorrow of parting and the transience of life. The voice of the female vocalist Kim Se-yoon is a crucial element that guides the flow of the piece, with her singing technique characterized by a harmonious blend of vocalization and traditional ornamentation. Kim Se-yoon articulates clearly while appropriately employing traditional embellishments to convey the melody. Her vocal volume is adeptly adjusted throughout the various sections of the piece, and her breath control is stable, allowing for a seamless flow even in longer phrases. Against the rhythm of the Doduri jangdan, her voice naturally rides the rhythm, enhancing the development of the piece by emphasizing each syllable. Kim Se-yoon's breath culminates the piece, contributing to the overall genre's completeness.

캡션(한국어): 해주 아리랑은 신민요 아리랑의 한 유형으로, 서도민요의 특징이 잘 드러나는 민속악 곡이다. 이 곡은 '아리아리 얼쑤'라는 후렴구로 잘 알려져 있으며, 경쾌하고 활기찬 분위기를 자아낸다. 여창 가창자 김민경의 목소리는 이 곡의 전개를 이끌어가는 중요한 요소로 작용한다. 그녀는 발성을 통해 곡의 멜로디를 명확하게 표현하며, 시김새를 적절히 활용하여 감정의 깊이를 더한다. 성량이 풍부하여 곡의 각 구절을 힘 있게 전달하며, 호흡을 조절하여 자연스럽고 안정된 흐름을 유지한다. 특히, 그녀의 호흡은 곡의 리듬에 잘 맞아떨어지며, 세마치 장단의 경쾌한 리듬 위에서 유연하게 흐른다. 김민경의 호흡은 곡의 마무리를 장식하며, 서도민요의 전통적인 요소를 잘 살려 장르적 완성도를 높인다. 이러한 요소들이 결합되어 해주 아리랑은 단순한 민요를 넘어서는 매력을 지닌 곡으로 완성된다.
캡션(영어): Haeju Arirang is a type of Sinminyo Arirang, a folk music piece that distinctly showcases the characteristics of Seodo Minyo. This song is well-known for its refrain "Ariari Eolsu," which evokes a lively and vibrant atmosphere. The voice of female vocalist Kim Min-kyung serves as a crucial element in the development of the piece. Through her vocalization, she clearly articulates the melody of the song and effectively employs techniques such as sigimsae to enhance the emotional depth. With her rich vocal timbre, she powerfully conveys each phrase of the piece while controlling her breath to maintain a natural and stable flow. Notably, her breathing aligns well with the rhythm of the song, flowing gracefully over the brisk rhythm of the semachi jangdan. Kim Min-kyung's breath adorns the conclusion of the piece, skillfully preserving the traditional elements of Seodo Minyo and elevating the genre's overall completeness. These elements combine to render Haeju Arirang a piece that transcends simple folk music, possessing a captivating charm.

캡션(영어): Dambangutaryeong is a Gyeongsangdo folk song that centers around tobacco, encapsulating the processes of planting and smoking tobacco as well as satire towards foreign powers. This piece serves as an exemplary representation of Gyeongsangdo folk music, with the refrain "dambanggu" being repeated to enhance its lively character. The voice of the female vocalist Kim Se-yoon acts as a core element driving the song forward. Kim Se-yoon adjusts her vocalization according to the structure of the piece, effectively conveying the unique emotions of the folk song through her use of sigimsae. Her vocal range varies throughout the progression of the song, and her ability to flow naturally with the gutgeori jangdan stands out. Kim Se-yoon skillfully manages her breath, allowing for appropriate pauses in each section of the melody, which further emphasizes the rhythmic quality of the piece. This control of breath also plays a crucial role in the conclusion of the song, contributing to the overall completeness of the genre.

캡션(한국어): 울산아가씨는 1930년대 이면상이 작곡하고 조영출이 작사한 신민요로, 경상도 민요풍의 선율을 바탕으로 울산 아가씨의 사랑과 애환을 노래하는 민속악의 한 형태이다. 이 곡은 경쾌한 템포와 해학적인 가사가 어우러지며, 경상도민요의 특징이 잘 드러나는 작품이다. 여창 가창자 김세윤의 목소리는 이 곡을 이끌어가는 중요한 요소로, 그녀의 발성은 전통적인 민요의 창법을 충실히 따르며, 시김새를 적절히 활용하여 멜로디의 흐름을 자연스럽게 이어간다. 김세윤은 곡의 각 구절에서 성량을 조절하며, 호흡을 통해 긴장감과 여유를 조화롭게 표현한다. 그녀의 목소리는 세마치 장단의 리듬에 맞춰 유연하게 흐르며, 각 음절을 명확하게 전달하면서도 곡의 전개에 따라 미세한 변화로 리듬감을 고조시킨다. 곡의 마무리 부분에서 김세윤은 호흡을 통해 여운을 남기며, 세마치의 경쾌한 리듬 위에서 곡의 완성도를 높인다. 이러한 요소들은 울산아가씨가 단순한 민요를 넘어서는 독특한 매력을 발산하게 한다.
캡션(영어): Ulsan Agassi is a new folk song composed by Lee Myun-sang and with lyrics by Jo Young-chul in the 1930s, which is a form of folk music that sings about the love and sorrows of the Ulsan maiden, based on the melodies of Gyeongsang-do folk songs. This piece features a lively tempo and humorous lyrics, showcasing the characteristics of Gyeongsang-do folk music effectively. The voice of the female vocalist Kim Se-yoon is a crucial element that drives the song, as her vocalization faithfully adheres to traditional folk singing techniques and appropriately utilizes vocal embellishments to create a natural flow in the melody. Kim Se-yoon adjusts her vocal volume in each phrase, harmoniously expressing tension and relaxation through her breath. Her voice flows flexibly with the rhythm of the semachi jangdan, clearly articulating each syllable while subtly enhancing the rhythmic feel according to the song's progression. In the concluding section, Kim Se-yoon leaves a lingering resonance through her breath, elevating the piece's completeness over the lively rhythm of the semachi. These elements contribute to Ulsan Agassi's unique charm that transcends a simple folk song.

캡션(영어): Yongcheonggeom is a Jeju folk song that features lyrics similar to those found in the Gyeonggi Bangataryeong, focusing on the theme of love between men and women. This piece is passed down through Jeju singers and, while influenced by mainland folk songs, effectively captures the unique emotional essence of Jeju. The voice of the female vocalist, Chae Su-hyun, conveys the song's theme effectively, showcasing delicate vocal techniques and nuances based on the traditional Jeju singing style. Her voice naturally expresses the melody, adjusting the dynamics of each syllable to convey emotion. Chae Su-hyun skillfully manages her breath to sustain long phrases, impressively introducing fluid changes in accordance with the melody's flow. Additionally, her singing rides the rhythm of the semachi jangdan, clearly revealing the structure of the piece. The vocalist's breath embellishes the conclusion of the song, enhancing the genre's completeness by preserving the traditional elements of Jeju folk music.
